paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for six different model configurations: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). The x-axis is labeled "#Iteration" and spans from 0 to 140,000 on a linear scale, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and ranges from approximately 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The Vanilla model is shown as a purple solid line that starts above 3.4 at iteration 0, drops steeply through the first 20,000 iterations, and then gradually decreases to approximately 2.45 by 140,000 iterations, achieving the lowest final loss among all lines. The StrmLLM (n=64) line is shown in blue and follows a similar steep initial decline but converges to a notably higher final loss of approximately 2.60 at 140,000 iterations. The SepLLM (n=64) line is shown in orange and decreases from above 3.4 to approximately 2.51–2.52 by 140,000 iterations. The SepLLM (n=64, H) line is shown in green and tracks very closely with the SepLLM (n=64) orange line, converging to a similar value near 2.51–2.52. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) line is shown in red and converges to approximately 2.49 by 140,000 iterations, reaching the lowest final loss among the SepLLM variants. The SepLLM (n=128) line is shown in dark blue and converges to approximately 2.55 at 140,000 iterations, settling between the StrmLLM line and the other SepLLM variants. All six lines exhibit their most rapid decrease in loss within the first approximately 20,000 iterations, after which the rate of decrease slows considerably and the curves flatten toward their respective final values. Each line appears to have a shaded region around it indicating variability or confidence bounds.
